-- Schema for database: rschema_0358

CREATE TABLE `scheduled_task` (
  `id` varchar(255) NOT NULL,
  `revision` varchar(255) NOT NULL,
  `type` varchar(255) NOT NULL,
  `lock_expiration_time` varchar(255) NOT NULL,
  `lock_owner` varchar(255) NOT NULL,
  `exclusive` varchar(255) NOT NULL,
  `execution_id` varchar(255) NOT NULL,
  `process_instance_id` varchar(255) NOT NULL,
  `process_definition_id` varchar(255) NOT NULL,
  `retries` varchar(255) NOT NULL,
  `exception_stack_id` varchar(255) NOT NULL,
  `exception_message` varchar(255) NOT NULL,
  `due_date` varchar(255) NOT NULL,
  `repeat` varchar(255) NOT NULL,
  `handler_type` varchar(255) NOT NULL,
  `handler_configuration` varchar(255) NOT NULL,
  `tenant_id` varchar(255) NOT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (`id`),
  CONSTRAINT `scheduled_task_ibfk_execution_id` FOREIGN KEY (`execution_id`) REFERENCES `execution_instance` (`execution_id`) ON DELETE CASCADE ON UPDATE CASCADE,
  CONSTRAINT `scheduled_task_ibfk_process_instance_id` FOREIGN KEY (`process_instance_id`) REFERENCES `execution_instance` (`process_instance_id`) ON DELETE CASCADE ON UPDATE CASCADE
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb3;

CREATE TABLE `execution_instance` (
  `execution_id` varchar(255) NOT NULL,
  `process_instance_id` varchar(255) NOT NULL,
  `process_definition_id` varchar(255) NOT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (`execution_id`)
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb3;
gold_question: Business requirements description of workflow management system: The system is used to manage complex business processes and supports the recording and monitoring of scheduled tasks and execution instances. Each scheduled task has a task ID, task type, lock information, execution instance ID, process instance ID, process definition ID, number of retries, exception information, expiration time, repeat configuration, processor configuration, and tenant ID. The system needs to record the execution of each task, including the start time, end time, execution result, and exception information of the task. Each execution of a task needs to be associated with an execution instance, which has an execution instance ID, process instance ID, and process definition ID. An execution instance can include the execution of multiple tasks. By recording the relationship between tasks and execution instances, the system can track the execution of each task and support task scheduling, retries, and exception handling. At the same time, the system needs to support multi-tenant scenarios to ensure the isolation of task data of different tenants.

The database named rschema_0358 is a task scheduling system. It contains two tables: scheduled_task and execution_instance.
The scheduled_task table represents tasks scheduled for execution. It has 17 columns: id, revision, type, lock_expiration_time, lock_owner, exclusive, execution_id, process_instance_id, process_definition_id, retries, exception_stack_id, exception_message, due_date, repeat, handler_type, handler_configuration, and tenant_id. All these columns allow null values and have a default value of null. The primary key of this table is the id column.
The execution_instance table represents instances of process executions. It has 3 columns: execution_id, process_instance_id, and process_definition_id. The primary key of this table is the execution_id column.
The scheduled_task table has two foreign keys: execution_id and process_instance_id. They reference the execution_id and process_instance_id columns of the execution_instance table respectively. The delete and update rules for these foreign keys are set to CASCADE, meaning that if a record in the execution_instance table is deleted or updated, the corresponding records in the scheduled_task table will also be deleted or updated.
This schema is used for managing tasks and their associated processes in a task scheduling system.
